html-i11-select-textarea.q: Your backend receives department=Billing question instead of the short code billing. What is wrong with the markup?
options: The select element is missing its name attribute
The chosen option has no value attribute, so the browser submitted its visible text
The option is missing the selected attribute
The optgroup label overrode the option's value
html-i11-select-textarea.why: Without a value attribute, an option falls back to submitting its display text. A value="billing" keeps the submitted token stable regardless of wording changes.

html-i11-select-textarea.q: You want a comment box that starts pre-filled with 'Type here...'. Which markup is correct?
options: <textarea name="c" value="Type here..."></textarea>
<textarea name="c" placeholder="Type here..." value="Type here...">
<textarea name="c">Type here...</textarea>
<textarea name="c" default="Type here..."></textarea>
html-i11-select-textarea.why: A textarea has no value attribute — its default text is its content, written between the opening and closing tags.

html-i11-select-textarea.q: A 'Show preview' helper button inside your form keeps submitting the form when clicked. Why?
options: Buttons inside forms always submit no matter what
The button is missing a name attribute
It was written as <button> with no type, which defaults to submit inside a form
It should have been an optgroup
html-i11-select-textarea.why: Inside a form, a button without an explicit type behaves as type="submit". Helper buttons need type="button".

html-i12-input-attributes.q: An order form shows the order number in a field the user must not edit, but the server still needs to receive it. Which attribute do you use?
options: disabled — it greys the field out
readonly — uneditable but still submitted
hidden — invisible and submitted
maxlength="0" — nothing more can be typed
html-i12-input-attributes.why: readonly blocks editing while keeping the field in the submission; disabled would exclude it from the submitted data entirely.

html-i12-input-attributes.q: Users can still type 50 characters into a username field you wrote as <input size="12">. What happened?
options: The browser ignored the attribute because it needs units
size only sets the visible width — maxlength is what caps input length
size must be combined with pattern to work
The field also needed spellcheck="false"
html-i12-input-attributes.why: size is purely visual sizing; only maxlength actually prevents typing past the limit.

html-i12-input-attributes.q: A verification-code field should raise a digits-only keypad on phones but must keep codes with leading zeros like 042518. What is the best markup?
options: <input type="number" name="otp">
<input type="text" name="otp" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code">
<input type="tel" name="otp" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="true">
<input type="range" name="otp" min="0" max="999999">
html-i12-input-attributes.why: type="text" preserves leading zeros, inputmode="numeric" requests the digit keypad, and autocomplete="one-time-code" lets mobile browsers suggest the incoming SMS code.

html-i13-validation.q: Users see only 'Please match the requested format' on your invite-code field and give up. What is the standard fix?
options: Replace pattern with minlength
Add a title attribute describing the expected format — it appears in the error bubble
Wrap the pattern in slashes so the browser can read it
Add novalidate to the form
html-i13-validation.why: The title attribute's text is appended to the browser's pattern error, turning a dead end into an instruction.

html-i13-validation.q: Your editors need to save half-finished articles, but the Publish flow must keep validating. Where does the attribute go?
options: novalidate on the form element
formnovalidate on the Save draft submit button
required="false" on the title input
disabled on the Publish button until the form is valid
html-i13-validation.why: formnovalidate skips validation only for submissions triggered by that specific button; novalidate on the form would also disable checks for Publish.

html-i13-validation.q: A colleague argues that with required, pattern and min/max in place, the server no longer needs validation. What is the correct response?
options: Correct — the browser guarantees the constraints before sending
Correct, as long as the form also uses method="post"
Wrong — client checks are trivially bypassed with DevTools or curl, so the server must re-validate everything
Wrong — but only pattern needs re-checking server-side
html-i13-validation.why: Client-side validation runs in software the sender controls and can be stripped or bypassed entirely; it is a UX layer, never a security boundary.

html-i14-datalist-output-meter.q: A city field should suggest common destinations but still accept any city a user types. Which element fits?
options: A select with all known cities
A datalist linked to the input via its list attribute
A select with multiple enabled
An output listing suggestions
html-i14-datalist-output-meter.why: A datalist offers suggestions without restricting input — unlike select, users can type values that are not listed.

html-i14-datalist-output-meter.q: You need to show that a file upload is 45% complete. Which markup is semantically correct?
options: <meter value="45" max="100"></meter>
<progress value="45" max="100"></progress>
<progress value="45"></progress>
<output value="45"></output>
html-i14-datalist-output-meter.why: Task completion is what progress means; and max="100" is needed because without it the scale runs 0 to 1 and 45 would render as full. Meter is for measurements, not tasks.

html-i14-datalist-output-meter.q: A disk-usage gauge should turn red as the disk fills. Which attribute set tells the browser that low values are the good zone?
options: value, min and max only
low, high and optimum, with optimum set near min
step set to a small number
kind="warning" on the meter
html-i14-datalist-output-meter.why: low and high divide the meter's range into zones, and a low optimum declares emptiness desirable — so the browser recolours the bar as the value climbs into the bad zone.

html-i15-video.q: You list a WebM and an MP4 source, but the browser ignores both and plays the file named in the video tag's src attribute. Why?
options: The sources were missing type attributes
When the video element has an src attribute, all source children are ignored
WebM must always be listed last
source elements need closing tags to register
html-i15-video.why: src on the video element and nested source children are mutually exclusive mechanisms — the attribute wins and the alternatives are never considered.

html-i15-video.q: Your muted hero video refuses to autoplay on phones. The markup is <video autoplay loop src="bg.mp4">. What is missing?
options: The controls attribute
The muted attribute — browsers block audible autoplay
preload="auto"
A poster image
html-i15-video.why: Autoplay policies require the muted attribute in the markup; without it most browsers simply never start playback, regardless of the file's actual audio.

html-i15-video.q: What does the type attribute on a source element actually buy you?
options: It forces the browser to transcode into that format
The browser can reject unsupported formats instantly without downloading any of the file
It is required or the video will not play
It enables the poster frame
html-i15-video.why: With a declared MIME type the browser decides support from the markup alone; without it, it must fetch part of each candidate file to sniff the format.

html-i16-audio-track.q: Your MP3 source is written as <source src="ep.mp3" type="audio/mp3"> and some browsers skip it. What is the correct type?
options: audio/mpeg — the registered MIME type for MP3
audio/mp3gain
music/mp3
application/mp3
html-i16-audio-track.why: MP3's registered MIME type is audio/mpeg; audio/mp3 is a common guess that browsers are not obliged to accept.

html-i16-audio-track.q: A viewer who is deaf needs the dialogue plus cues like [door slams]. Which track kind serves them?
options: subtitles — translated dialogue
captions — speech plus meaningful non-speech sounds
descriptions — narration of visuals
metadata — cues for scripts
html-i16-audio-track.why: Captions target people who cannot hear the audio, so they include non-speech information; subtitles assume the viewer hears sound but needs the language.

html-i16-audio-track.q: A track element points at a correct .vtt file but no captions ever appear. The file starts directly with the first cue timing. What is wrong?
options: Cue timings must use commas, not periods
The file is missing the mandatory WEBVTT header line, so the whole track fails to parse
The track needs a type="text/vtt" attribute
Captions only work on video, never with valid markup
html-i16-audio-track.why: A WebVTT file must begin with the literal line WEBVTT; without it, browsers silently discard the entire track.

html-i17-iframes-embeds.q: An accessibility audit flags every iframe on your site. The frames have src, width and height. What is most likely missing?
options: The sandbox attribute
The title attribute — without it screen readers announce only 'frame'
loading="lazy"
The name attribute
html-i17-iframes-embeds.why: Screen-reader users need the title's description to know what a frame contains; an untitled frame is announced with no context at all.

html-i17-iframes-embeds.q: You embed an untrusted third-party widget that only needs to run its own JavaScript to draw a chart. What is the right sandbox?
options: No sandbox — the iframe is isolated anyway
sandbox="allow-scripts" — grant only what it needs
sandbox="allow-scripts allow-top-navigation allow-popups"
sandbox="" with allowfullscreen
html-i17-iframes-embeds.why: Sandbox works by granting the minimum tokens the embed needs; allow-scripts alone lets it draw while denying popups, form submission and navigation of your tab.

html-i17-iframes-embeds.q: You iframe a bank's login page for convenience and it renders blank. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Login pages need allow="camera" to render
The bank's server sends X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers that forbid framing, to prevent clickjacking
iframes cannot load HTTPS content
The iframe is missing a name attribute
html-i17-iframes-embeds.why: Sites protect sensitive pages with framing headers so hostile pages cannot overlay and hijack clicks on them — the blank frame is the defence working.

html-i18-computercode.q:
Documentation must show the literal markup

Hello

to readers, but it keeps vanishing from the rendered page. What fixes it?
options: Wrap it in samp instead of code
Write the angle brackets as < and > so they display instead of parsing
Add spellcheck="false" to the pre element
Use two pre elements nested
html-i18-computercode.why: Raw < and > are parsed as real tags; the < and > entities render the symbols as visible text.

html-i18-computercode.q: A terminal transcript mixes commands the reader types and responses the machine prints. Which pairing is semantically correct?
options: code for both, styled differently
kbd for the typed commands, samp for the printed output
samp for the typed commands, kbd for the printed output
var for commands, code for output
html-i18-computercode.why: kbd marks human-to-machine input and samp marks machine-to-human output — the direction of flow decides the element.

html-i18-computercode.q: In the usage line ssh user@host, readers must replace user and host with their own values. How do you mark those two words?
options: user — bold shows importance
<var>user</var> — var marks placeholders the reader substitutes
<samp>user</samp> — it is sample text
<kbd>user</kbd> — the user types it
html-i18-computercode.why: var is the element for variables and placeholders; it tells readers exactly which parts of an example are theirs to replace.

html-i19-responsive-basics.q: Your carefully written min-width media queries never trigger on phones — the site renders as a tiny desktop miniature. What is missing?
options: A max-width query for phones
The viewport meta tag with width=device-width — without it the browser simulates a ~980px canvas
px units instead of rem in the queries
loading="lazy" on the images
html-i19-responsive-basics.why: Without the viewport tag, mobile browsers report a fake desktop width, so narrow-screen media queries never match and the page is scaled down instead.

html-i19-responsive-basics.q: After adding width: 100% to all images, small icons render blurry and huge. What should the rule have been?
options: height: 100% as well
max-width: 100% with height: auto — shrink to fit but never enlarge
min-width: 100%
width: auto with no height
html-i19-responsive-basics.why: max-width only constrains images that exceed their container; width: 100% force-stretches every image, inflating small ones past their natural size.

html-i19-responsive-basics.q: A user increases their browser's default font size but your site's text does not budge. Which sizing choice caused this?
options: Text sized in rem units
Text sized in fixed px values, which ignore the user's preference
Text sized in percentages
The missing lang attribute
html-i19-responsive-basics.why: rem scales from the root font size, which follows the user's browser setting; fixed px sizes override that preference entirely.

html-i20-project-registration.q: A registration form was shipped with method="get" and users' emails are appearing in server access logs. Why does switching to post fix this?
options: POST encrypts the data automatically
GET appends form data to the URL, which gets logged, cached and shared; POST carries it in the request body
GET limits forms to five fields
POST validates fields before sending
html-i20-project-registration.why: GET serialises submissions into the query string, exposing personal data everywhere URLs travel; POST moves the data into the request body (though HTTPS is still what encrypts it).

html-i20-project-registration.q: Testers report they can select Standard, Student and Speaker tickets simultaneously. The radios are named ticket1, ticket2, ticket3. What went wrong?
options: Radios need the multiple attribute removed
Mutual exclusivity comes from a shared name — all three must be name="ticket"
Each radio needs required
The radios must share one id
html-i20-project-registration.why: The browser groups radios by their name attribute; distinct names create three independent one-button groups that can all be on at once.

html-i20-project-registration.q: Attendees may sign up for any number of optional workshops. Which control is the right choice?
options: Radio buttons sharing one name
A group of checkboxes sharing a name, one per workshop
A select with multiple, relying on Ctrl-click
A required select with one workshop per option
html-i20-project-registration.why: Checkboxes natively express zero-to-many choices with obvious interaction; multiple selects depend on a Ctrl-click convention many users do not know, and radios force exactly one.
